clue.text: Not favouring money share out application

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against or not in favour
a cent is a small coin, standing for money
to ration is to share out in fixed portions

explanation.surface: A request to have money divided up is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' looks like a form to fill in, but here it means mental effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Application in the sense of diligent focused attention is a synonym for mental focus of this kind.

clue.text: Making a speech is nothing to a seafaring man

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a rating is a naval sailor below officer rank

explanation.surface: A sailor cares nothing for speechmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ... to' joins the two pieces: O placed before the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address, so the present participle means delivering a speech.

clue.text: Burn where there's fish

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out where fish are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch something is to char it, and the char is a trout-like freshwater fish.

clue.text: Most systematic and bovine creatures set at odds

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle

indicators.note: letters at odds with each other are out of their proper order, so the word set is scrambled

explanation.surface: Cattle are placed in conflict with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT, meaning cattle, is an old word the solver may not know; 'at odds' scrambles the three-letter word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy and orderly, so the superlative describes the most orderly arrangement.

clue.text: Hit the drink to get sympathy

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
port is a fortified wine, and in crosswords the drink is often port

explanation.surface: Someone takes to the bottle in search of fellow feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the drink' reads as taking to alcohol, but it splits into a blow and a fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close harmonious understanding between people, which is mutual sympathy.

clue.text: Duck leaves lake

parts.note: tea is made from dried leaves
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A duck flies off from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departure, but it is the noun for tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling bird of that family.

clue.text: Last longer in general without wearying

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words without wearying, so in signals a run concealed there

explanation.surface: Something durable keeps going in general without tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across witHOUT WEARying; 'general' merely pads the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to outlast it, lasting longer than it does in use.

clue.text: Meaningless but popular device if one is not able

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sign is an emblem or heraldic device
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
can't, written without the apostrophe, means is not able

explanation.surface: A gadget that is fashionable but useless if a person cannot operate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial and of no importance lacks significance, so it carries no meaning or weight.

clue.text: Could be tried, people agree, though with some prejudice

indicators.note: the word tried could be rearranged into another form, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: men stands for people in general
two accounts that tally agree with each other

explanation.surface: In a trial, a jury agrees but with a bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting harmfully or to someone's disadvantage is acting with prejudice in its legal sense of damage.

clue.text: Falls back again, meeting men with guns

indicators.note: the word again is read backwards, as if going back

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles again when meeting armed soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb, but it is the noun naming the waterfall; 'back' turns the word again round to give NIAGA, and 'meeting' joins the gunners after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the US-Canada border bear this name.

clue.text: Coin for a priest's use

indicators.note: putting the letters to new use reshapes them into a different word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A clergyman has some money set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' asks for the letters of A PRIEST to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A piastre is a monetary unit of Egypt, Syria and other countries, a kind of coin.

clue.text: A girl making a bloomer

explanation.surface: A young woman makes an embarrassing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a girl's name, and it is also a flowering plant, something that blooms.

clue.text: Flier having a bit of bother-only to be expected

indicators.note: only a portion of the letters in bother-only is taken, so the run sits within them

explanation.surface: A traveller has a little trouble, which is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird runs across botHER ONly; 'to be expected' merely pads the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is anything that flies, and this wading bird is one.

clue.text: Cherished at great cost

explanation.surface: Something loved is bought at a high price.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means beloved, and also expensive.

clue.text: Clock up mail

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a timer is a clock for measuring intervals

explanation.surface: The postal service's clock records the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock up' looks like a phrase for recording, but 'up' reverses TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send money by post, so it means to mail payment.

clue.text: A swimmer's rude gesture

explanation.surface: Someone in the water makes an insulting sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The snook is a sea fish, and cocking a snook is thumbing one's nose, an insulting gesture.

clue.text: Get clean perhaps, relinquishing a certain slovenliness

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of get clean might form something else

parts.note: the letter a is taken away from the anagram's pool

explanation.surface: Someone stops washing and lets themselves go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relinquishing' takes A from GETCLEAN; the rest rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is careless failure to attend to things, which is a form of untidiness or laziness.

clue.text: So much French spirit and temper!

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A Frenchman drinks too much and loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of bad temper.

clue.text: Fussy type taking tot in hand

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so in signals the hand closes round the sum

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A fusspot is holding a small child by the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child, but it means add up.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddist follows food or health fads obsessively, a fussy particular person.

clue.text: To sack a large number is to be unsuccessful

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
taken as written
to miss is to fail to hit, to be unsuccessful

explanation.surface: Firing lots of workers is a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone is to fire them from employment.

clue.text: Musical instrument of distinctive tone a learner wanted

parts.note: timbre is the characteristic quality of a sound
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A trainee is sought to play an instrument with a characteristic sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbrel is an ancient tambourine, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Carried in front of a Scotsman

definitions.text: Carried in front of a Scotsman

parts.words: Carried in front of a Scotsman
parts.note: a Highland pouch worn at the front of a kilt, read as if something were borne in procession ahead of a man

explanation.surface: Something is borne ahead of a Scot in procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is a pouch worn hanging in front of the kilt in Highland dress.

clue.text: With very little cash about, the queen is thoughtful

indicators.note: about means around, so the coins wrap the queen

parts.note: sous are French coins of tiny value, so very little cash
ER I is the royal cipher of Elizabeth the First, a queen

explanation.surface: Someone with almost no money considers the monarch carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious means grave and earnest, given to deep reflection.

clue.text: Don't have an arbitrator come down

parts.note: a ref, a referee, is an arbitrator in sport
rain is what comes down from the sky

explanation.surface: An umpire is told not to get caught in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Refrain as an imperative verb means abstain or hold back, which is saying don't.

clue.text: All the players appear shy

explanation.surface: Every actor seems timid.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast is the full company of actors, and to shy something is to throw or cast it.

clue.text: It doesn't hurt to be well turned out!

definitions.text: It doesn't hurt to be well turned out!

parts.words: It doesn't hurt to be well turned out!
parts.note: a playful line on a word that means both to sting with pain and to be neatly dressed

explanation.surface: Dressing well never did anyone any harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means stylishly dressed, and as a verb it means to sting, a kind of pain.

clue.text: No longer available to a dyke builder

parts.note: an item off the menu is no longer available

explanation.surface: An embankment builder can't be reached any more.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFA was an 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke, an earthwork along the English-Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: This Anglo-Saxon king gave his name to the great earthwork he had constructed.

clue.text: Painter with caged male bird

indicators.note: a caged thing is enclosed, so the painter surrounds the male

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: An artist keeps a male bird in a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird similar to an ostrich.

clue.text: A time for style

explanation.surface: Now is the moment for fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed period, such as a school session, and to term something is to name or style it.

clue.text: Not one may be found therein

indicators.note: the letters of therein may be found rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Nothing may be discovered inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be found' asks for the letters of THEREIN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Neither means not either of two, so not one of the pair.

clue.text: Concerning everybody, generally speaking

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A general remark applies to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall as an adverb means taken as a whole, on the whole.

clue.text: This bent male's the making of the firm!

indicators.note: the making of something forms it from raw material, so these letters are built into a new word

explanation.surface: A crooked businessman is what built the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like an anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'the making of' rearranges THIS BENT MALES.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment is a business or company, the same as a commercial firm.
